severity: HIGH — a real, silent violation of Engine Spec §9.3/PRD OQ-3's own guarantee ('overriding it would resurrect text a colleague deliberately removed'), reachable via entirely ordinary use of the shipped undo/redo feature (no fault injection, no reconnection, no GC horizon involved)
oneLineDescription: Undo of a LOCAL insert that a peer has already deleted (Test Plan UNDO-06 / PRD FR-CE-12) mints an idempotent Delete per Engine Spec §9.2 ('possibly advances deletedBy... THE DOCUMENT IS UNCHANGED') — but applyDelete's own correct, necessary max-wins attribution logic silently reassigns deletedBy to the UNDOING replica as a side effect of that 'harmless' idempotent delete. A LATER redo of that same undo then mints an Undelete which satisfies Engine Spec §4.6's replica-equality check against that newly-reassigned attribution, resurrecting content a third party legitimately and independently deleted — exactly the outcome OQ-3 exists to forbid.
discoveredDuring: Phase 36 implementation, writing the engine-level UNDO-07 (redo-symmetry) test for the UNDO-06 scenario (undo of an insert already deleted by someone else). The test's own redo assertion failed: text came back as the original character instead of staying empty.

mechanism.step1: Replica A inserts 'x' (opA). Replica B deletes it independently (delOpB, target=opA.id). A applies delOpB: A's own local state is now deleted, deletedBy=delOpB.id (B).
mechanism.step2: A undoes ITS OWN original insert (Engine Spec §9.1, case 'insert' -> Delete{target: op.id}). A mints a fresh Delete (invD1, replica A) and applies it. applyDelete's general, CORRECT, necessary causally-latest-wins logic (Engine Spec §4.5, used identically for every concurrent delete in the system) compares invD1 against the CURRENT deletedBy (delOpB, B) — since invD1 is a freshly minted identifier, its counter always exceeds every counter this replica has already observed, so invD1 UNCONDITIONALLY WINS the comparison and deletedBy silently becomes invD1 (A) — even though the node's `deleted` flag itself does not change (it was already `true`). Engine Spec §9.2 explicitly sanctions this exact side effect as harmless in isolation: 'This sets deleted <- true (already true) and possibly advances deletedBy... THE DOCUMENT IS UNCHANGED.'
mechanism.step3: A later redoes that same undo (Engine Spec §9.4: 'for an insert-then-undo, this is an Undelete of the original node'). A mints a fresh Undelete (invU1, replica A) targeting opA.id and applies it. Engine Spec §4.6's own rule fires: 'if n.deletedBy.replica = op.by' — deletedBy is now invD1 (A, from step 2's silent reassignment) and op.by is A (the redo's own replica) — THEY MATCH — so the node is resurrected (deleted <- false), even though the CONTENT-LEVEL reason it was deleted was always B's own, entirely separate, still-standing deletion.
mechanism.consequence: The document shows the resurrected character again, silently overriding B's legitimate, independent deletion — with no fault injection, no reconnection, and no interaction with garbage collection or the undo horizon required. This is a direct violation of OQ-3's own stated justification: 'Overriding it would resurrect text a colleague deliberately removed, into a document they are still editing.'

minimalReproduction.description: Fully deterministic, no real time or network required. Verified passing (asserting the FIXED behavior) as packages/engine/src/engine.test.ts's own 'UNDO-06 (FR-CE-12)' + its UNDO-07 redo-symmetry follow-up, and as a dedicated permanent regression test, packages/engine/src/regressionR0014.test.ts (in the default pnpm test suite).
minimalReproduction.engineConstruction: Two Engine instances, replica A (id 10) and replica B (id 20).

operationStreamPreFix.note: PRE-FIX: applyDelete's max-wins logic silently reassigns deletedBy to {c:3,r:10} (A) here. a.text() is still '' (no visible change), matching UNDO-06's own expectation in isolation.

operationStreamPreFix.result: PRE-FIX (BUG): { kind: 'applied', operation: { kind: 'undelete', id: {c:4,r:10}, target: {c:1,r:10} } }, a.text() === 'x'
operationStreamPreFix.note: WRONG — resurrects content B legitimately deleted, because deletedBy.r (A, from the undo's own silent reassignment) now matches this Undelete's own op.id.r (A).

operationStreamPostFix.note: Same wire operation as before (§9.2 is still followed literally — a real Delete is still minted, applied, and transmitted) — but the engine now ALSO records, internally, that this specific application had NO visible effect (deleted was already true before and after).

operationStreamPostFix.result: FIXED: { kind: 'applied', operation: { kind: 'delete', id: {c:4,r:10}, target: {c:1,r:10} } }, a.text() === ''
operationStreamPostFix.note: CORRECT — because the entry being reversed is known to have been a no-op, redo mints ANOTHER DELETE (repeating the same kind), never an Undelete, so it can never resurrect anything. B's independent deletion is never overridden.

fix.summary: Engine.undo()/redo() now track, per stack entry, whether that entry's own application actually changed the target's visible (`deleted`) state (`hadEffect: boolean`, captured via a before/after comparison at apply time) — not just the entry's operation KIND. Reversing an entry with `hadEffect: true` uses the standard Engine Spec §9.1/§9.4 kind-based inverse mapping (unchanged from the original implementation, and still fully subject to Engine Spec §4.6/OQ-3's own replica-equality check for legitimate cases). Reversing an entry with `hadEffect: false` instead REPEATS the same operation kind (delete->delete, undelete->undelete) rather than inverting it — this can never mint the 'dangerous' opposite-kind operation that could newly succeed due to attribution drift, so a known no-op faithfully stays a no-op through arbitrarily many further undo/redo cycles of that same entry.
fix.verifiedAgainst: The full new Phase 36 undo/redo test suite (packages/engine/src/engine.test.ts, UNDO-01 through UNDO-11, all with UNDO-07 redo-symmetry checks where applicable) — confirmed the fix is ADDITIVE PRECISION, not a behavior change, for every already-correct case (UNDO-01/03/04/05/09, all of which have `hadEffect: true` on every transition that matters, or — for UNDO-04's own OQ-3 no-op branch — were never vulnerable in the first place, since applyUndelete's own no-op branch, unlike applyDelete's, never mutates `deletedBy` at all).

whyThisIsDifferentFromR0008ThroughR0013: R0008-R0011 were defects in the CRDT placement/ordering algorithm itself (YATA-family, since replaced by Fugue); R0012/R0013 concern tombstone garbage-collection eligibility and its interaction with a live client. This is neither — Engine.applyDelete's max-wins attribution and Engine.applyUndelete's §4.6 replica-equality check are EACH individually correct, exactly as specified. This is an emergent interaction between two individually-correct, individually-specified rules (§9.2's 'advancing deletedBy is harmless' and §4.6's OQ-3 check) that neither rule's own text addresses when COMPOSED across an undo followed by a later redo — the kind of finding only surfaces by actually building and exercising the full undo/redo round trip the Test Plan's own UNDO-07 item requires, not by reviewing either rule in isolation.
reproducibilityCaveat: None — this fully satisfies Test Plan §2.3 Rule 3 (a complete, byte-exact, deterministic operation stream). No fault injection, timing, network, or randomness of any kind is required to reproduce it, before or after the fix.
